---
title: "Data quality"
---

*Status: v0.1 (milestone M2 in progress). This is the project's running
register of known problems with the
[data sources](data-sources.qmd). It is expected to grow as sources are
ingested in earnest.*

## What this report covers

The [roadmap](../ROADMAP.md) asks for a register of **known gaps,
revisions, suppressions, and definitional breaks**. Anything that would
mislead a reader who trusted a number at face value belongs here.

## Known gaps

- **Determinants and stratifiers.** Income, education, and employment are
  used to stratify results (see the
  [measurement framework](measurement-framework.qmd)); BC Stats, the BC
  Data Catalogue, Statistics Canada, and K-12 reporting are catalogued as
  their sources. They are **determinants, not health outcomes**, and are
  never reported as health on their own.
- **Microdata access.** Individual-level sources are catalogued as
  [access routes](data-sources.qmd#microdata-access-routes) (Population
  Data BC; Statistics Canada Research Data Centres) but no approvals are
  in place yet, so the catalogue is aggregate-only in practice. Nothing
  individual-level may enter the repository regardless.
- **Neighbourhood-level health indicators.** Population denominators exist
  at LHA/neighbourhood resolution, but health outcomes are not yet
  catalogued below health-authority level.
- **External drivers.** Cross-border patient flows and supply-chain
  pressures are identified as relevant but have **no catalogued source**
  yet; the wildfire, demographic, and macro series are the current
  stand-ins.
- **Social wellbeing.** Measures of social connection and belonging are
  sparse and carried on a small number of survey series only.

## Revisions and provisional figures

- **Substance-use mortality** is published provisionally and revised
  upward as investigations conclude [@bccdcDrugs]. Preliminary and final
  figures must never be pooled without noting the vintage.
- **Cancer statistics** for the most recent years are typically incomplete
  because of registration lag [@bcCancer].
- **Population estimates** at sub-provincial levels are revised as
  administrative sources update; rates computed on them inherit the
  revision.
- **National survey estimates** carry sampling error and are occasionally
  revised after release [@statcan].

## Suppression

- **Small-area counts** (e.g. vital statistics by small geography) are
  suppressed for privacy [@bcStatsVital]. Suppressed cells are missing,
  not zero; treating them as zero biases rates.

## Definitional breaks (regime shifts)

These are candidates for the **regime-aware reporting** required by
milestone M3; each marks a point where a series before and after is
effectively different. The pipeline dates regime breaks from the data
itself (piecewise-linear segmentation with BIC selection, plus a
permutation test for a break beyond a linear trend); the table below
records the *known causes* behind such breaks, which the statistical
test can locate but cannot name.

The within-versus-across-regime split in the report is made inferential
with a Chow-style F-test of equal slopes either side of each dated break
[@chow1960]. It assumes the piecewise-linear form holds and that the
residuals are homoscedastic and independent — plausible for smooth annual
series, less so for the short pooled survey windows, which is why the
test is reported only where a break was actually selected. A significant
F means the *pace* of movement changed at the break, not merely the level.

| Break | Affected sources | Implication |
|-------|------------------|-------------|
| Cause-of-death coding revisions (ICD revisions) | Vital Statistics; national mortality | Cause-specific mortality series are not directly comparable across the revision boundary [@whoIcd] |
| Declared public-health emergency (2016) | BCCDC substance-use dashboard; overdose response | Surveillance expanded at the emergency; counts before and after reflect different detection intensity [@bcOverdoseEmergency2016] |
| COVID-19 pandemic (2020–) | mortality, morbidity, mental health | Both a real shock and a measurement shock (care disruption, coding changes) [@bcCovidEmergency; @whocovid] |
| Survey redesigns (e.g. Canadian Community Health Survey) | Statistics Canada health series | Break in trend; pre- and post-redesign estimates differ [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| Indicator-definition updates | CIHI indicators | Rebased or redefined indicators reset their own series [@cihi] |

## URL verification

As part of M2, every catalogued URL was checked for reachability with
`uv run sohbc check --all`. All catalogued landing pages and the
automated download endpoints returned HTTP 200 at the time of checking
(28 sources; the catalogue has since grown to 30 with the two regional
survey and life-expectancy tables). The federal publisher's own portal was
unreachable from the
verification environment, so federal open data is reached through the
Open Government portal record instead; this is noted on that catalogue
entry.

## First published indicator

The first end-to-end indicator — provincial
[mortality rates](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd) from Statistics
Canada table 13-10-0710-01 — is built by the pipeline, including
male/female breakdowns and per-sex age standardisation. Its known
limitations (provincial resolution only, source sex categories, spans
the COVID-19 period, subject to revision) are recorded on the indicator
page and are examples of the kind of entry this register is meant to
capture. Its regime breaks are dated by the formal tests documented on
that page rather than read off by eye.

A second indicator, [life expectancy at birth](indicator-life-expectancy-bc.qmd)
by sex (Statistics Canada table 13-10-0837-01), is now built through the
same pipeline; it shares the mortality domain and the same caveat
classes (period measure, revision of recent years, COVID-19 period,
source sex categories). The source table has no sub-provincial rows.

A third source, Statistics Canada table 13-10-0905-01, supplies a family
of survey indicators that widen the framework beyond mortality:
[life satisfaction](indicator-life-satisfaction-bc.qmd) and [mental
health](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd) series among them. Survey
estimates bring caveat classes the administrative tables did not:
sampling error, coefficient-of-variation suppression (flagged cells), and
a collection-frame change mid-series, so a step in the series may be a
step in the measurement. These are recorded on the indicator pages.

A fourth source takes the project below the province: Statistics Canada
table 13-10-0931-01 supplies [age-standardised premature and potentially
avoidable mortality](indicator-mortality-inequality-bc.qmd) for BC's five
health authorities and 16 health service delivery areas. It adds two
caveat classes of its own — health-region boundaries that change across
table vintages, and rates published only as overlapping **three-year
averages**, so the source supports a regional snapshot but not a regional
trajectory; the trend machinery is therefore not applied to it.

Sub-provincial coverage then widened to two more sources. Statistics
Canada table 13-10-0389-01 gives [regional life
expectancy](indicator-life-expectancy-regions-bc.qmd) for the five
authorities and 16 service delivery areas, but only to the 2015/2017
period and on the 2018 boundary set: it is a **pre-pandemic baseline** on
**different boundaries** from the mortality-inequality view, so the two
never pool. It also publishes **overlapping** three-year periods (ten
points sharing two years each), which makes the trend and break tests
overpowered — a caveat worth remembering whenever a pooled series is fed
to tests that assume independent observations. Statistics Canada table
13-10-0972-01 gives the survey family at service-delivery-area resolution
as **five pooled two-year periods** with heavier suppression than the
provincial table; with five points the stationarity verdict is
*undetermined* throughout, cells flagged *too unreliable to publish* are
kept in the tidy file but dropped from summaries, the indicator
*has a regular healthcare provider* is absent, and anxiety disorder is
missing from the most recent period.

## Governance

- **Licences vary** by source (open-government licences to publisher
  terms). Each catalogue entry records its licence; redistribution of
  anything committed must respect it.
- **No individual-level data** in the repository — a hard rule.
- **First Nations data** are governed by the First Nations principles of
  OCAP® and specific agreements; they are cited for context, not
  redistributed [@fnigcOcap].
- **"Best use" standard.** A source backed only by published summary
  statistics is admissible when it passes licence and governance checks —
  the goal is the best use of all publicly available information that can
  be appropriately used.

## Keeping this current

Add an entry here whenever ingesting a source surfaces a problem, and
update the [catalogue](data-sources.qmd) when a gap closes. See
[How to ingest a source](../how-to/ingest-data.qmd).
